content: Cardiotrophin-like cytokine factor 1 (CLCF1), also referred to as Novel Neurotrophin-1 (NNT-1) or B cell-stimulating factor-3 (BSF-3), is a protein encoded by the CLCF1 gene in humans. CLCF1 plays a role in inducing tyrosine phosphorylation of the IL-6 receptor common subunit glycoprotein 130 (gp130), the leukemia inhibitory factor receptor beta, and the transcription factor STAT3. It has been implicated in the induction of interleukin-1 (IL-1) through the stimulation of corticosterone and IL-6, as well as in the production of serum amyloid A and the proliferation of B cells. This cytokine is capable of activating B cells via stimulation of the gp130 receptor. Structurally, CLCF1 is a cytokine that belongs to the interleukin-6 (IL-6) family. It is a secreted protein predominantly found in lymph nodes and the spleen. The mature form of CLCF1 consists of 225 amino acids and has a molecular mass of 22 kDa. Members of the IL-6 family share similarities in their gene structure and exhibit a four-helix bundle in their protein structure. CLCF1 is closely related to other proteins, such as cardiotrophin-1 and ciliary neurotrophic factor.
